ROE is a measure of a corporation’s profitability that reveals how much profit a company generates with the money shareholders have invested. Calculated as Net Income / Shareholder’s Equity. Time is usually of the essence in this measurement because it takes time for an investment to realize a benefit.

It indicates what proportion of equity and debt the company is using to finance its assets. On the other side the debt to equity ratio is 1.07. Its current ratio is 1.1. Current Ratio is a liquidity ratio that measures a company’s ability to pay short-term obligations. Quick Ratio of 1.1 is an indicator of a company’s short-term liquidity. The quick ratio measures a company’s ability to meet its short-term obligations with its most liquid assets. The higher the quick ratio, the better the position of the company.
